purpose: Shared reference cases for phone vision tests (phone/TEST_PLAN.md). Offline orientation use case: no photo leaves the phone.
system_prompt: You are a helpful, concise assistant running offline on a phone. Answer briefly and accurately.
output_format: free text; no JSON grammar or schema is used (EngineBenchmark passes grammar: nil)
photo_notes: Photos are taken by hand on the day, saved as <file> next to this JSON in the app's Documents/golden/, EXIF intact. Fill ground_truth from what is physically visible before running any model.

cases.description: Photograph a London street-name plate (white or black plate with the street name, often with borough and a postcode district) square-on from 2 to 4 m, daylight, text readable by eye.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. What street name is on the sign in this photo? Reply in one sentence.
expected_key_facts: The street name printed on the plate

rubric.usable_if: Every must_mention item is present in the answer (case-insensitive; a one-character spelling slip is accepted) AND no must_not item applies.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Gives a different street name from the plate.
Adds a postcode or borough that is not printed.

cases.description: Photograph a Tube station entrance with the roundel and the station name visible, daylight, taken from the pavement opposite.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. Which Underground station entrance is this? Reply in one sentence.
expected_key_facts: Station name on the roundel or fascia

rubric.usable_if: Every must_mention item is present in the answer (case-insensitive; a one-character spelling slip is accepted) AND no must_not item applies.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Names a different station.
Names Tube lines that are not shown on any sign in the photo.

cases.description: Photograph one well-known landmark visible from a public place near the venue (a named tower, bridge, church or station facade), whole building in frame, daylight.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. What landmark is this, and which way would I be facing if I can see it from where I stand? Reply in two sentences.

ground_truth.facing_direction_if_known: (optional; compass bearing of the camera, measured by hand)

expected_key_facts: If a facing direction is given it matches ground truth within one compass octant (45 degrees)

rubric.usable_if: Every must_mention item is present in the answer (case-insensitive; a one-character spelling slip is accepted) AND no must_not item applies.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Names a different landmark.
Gives a compass direction when facing_direction_if_known is blank (invented), or one that is more than 45 degrees from the measured bearing.
rubric.notes: A landmark name alone is usable; a direction is only judged if the model gives one.

cases.description: Photograph a London bus stop sign (flag or shelter panel) showing the stop name, stop letter and route numbers, daylight.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. Read the bus stop sign. What is the stop name and which bus routes stop here? Reply briefly.
expected_key_facts: Route numbers listed on the sign

rubric.usable_if: Every must_mention item is present in the answer (case-insensitive; a one-character spelling slip is accepted) AND no must_not item applies.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Lists a route number that is not on the sign.
Gives a different stop name.

cases.description: Photograph a printed street map or Tube map on a pavement or station wall (for example a 'You are here' map), the whole panel in frame, text legible by eye.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. This is a printed map. What does it show, and what is the name of the marked 'You are here' point or the nearest labelled street or station?
expected_key_facts: A label that is printed on the map near the marked position

rubric.usable_if: Every must_mention item is present in the answer (case-insensitive; a one-character spelling slip is accepted) AND no must_not item applies.
must_mention: type of map (street map or Tube map) matches {map_type}
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Describes a labelled place that is not on the map.
Claims a precise position or direction on the map that the photo does not show.
rubric.notes: If the map has no 'You are here' marker, set ground truth to a street label that is clearly readable; do not require a position.

cases.description: Photograph a shop front with its name and a street number or address visible on the fascia or door, daylight.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. Read this shop front. What is the shop's name, and what address or street number is shown? Reply in one sentence.
expected_key_facts: Number or address text printed on the front

rubric.usable_if: Every must_mention item is present in the answer (case-insensitive; a one-character spelling slip is accepted) AND no must_not item applies.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Gives a different number (digits wrong).
Invents a street name that is not printed anywhere in the photo.
rubric.notes: Digits are checked exactly: a wrong digit makes the answer unusable.

cases.description: Photograph a sign (street plate or shop name) at dusk, at night, or in a dim underpass, no flash, text still readable by eye.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. What does the sign in this dark photo say? If you cannot read it, say so.
expected_key_facts: Sign text if the model can read it
Otherwise an honest statement that it is too dark

rubric.usable_if: Usable if the answer matches sign_text, OR honestly says it cannot read it and does not guess. A wrong guess is unusable.
must_mention: {sign_text}, OR an explicit statement that the text cannot be read reliably
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Presents a guess as certain when the text is wrong.

cases.description: Take a street-name plate or shop fascia with the phone held in landscape (or upside down) so the JPEG carries an EXIF orientation other than 1 (the file shows upright in the Photos app). Do NOT rotate or re-save it. Record the EXIF orientation value.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. What does the sign in this photo say? Reply in one sentence.
expected_key_facts: Sign text as it reads upright

rubric.usable_if: Usable if the answer matches sign_text. An answer saying the image is sideways or upside down and failing to read it is unusable.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Says the image is rotated, sideways or upside down (means the app did not apply the EXIF orientation).
Reads mirrored or partial text as if complete.
rubric.notes: Exercises ImagePrep's orientation fix. A failure here with the same file passing on the Spark (auto-oriented copy) is an orientation bug, not a model limit.

cases.description: Photograph a busy street scene with at least 4 different signs or labels in frame (market, high street at a junction), daylight.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. List the signs or place names you can read in this photo. Only list text you can actually read.
expected_key_facts: Two or more of the signs that are readable by eye

rubric.usable_if: Usable if at least 2 listed signs are in readable_signs and none of the listed signs is invented.
must_not: States as fact any street, station, landmark, number or text that is not visible in the photo (read the photo, not the model).
Lists any sign that is not in the photo.
Merges text from two signs into one.
rubric.notes: Partial lists are fine; invented items are not.

cases.description: Photograph something with no orienting information: a blank wall, the pavement, the sky, or a hand over the lens. No text, no recognisable building.
cases.prompt: I am lost in London and have no signal. Where am I? Which street or landmark is this? If you cannot tell from the photo, say so.
expected_key_facts: May describe only what is visible (wall, sky, pavement)

rubric.usable_if: Usable only if the answer honestly says it cannot tell and gives no place name.
must_mention: States that the photo does not show enough to say where the user is (words such as cannot tell, not enough information, no visible sign or landmark)
must_not: Names any street, station, landmark, borough or area.
Gives a direction or location with confidence.
rubric.notes: Any confident place name is unusable, even a plausible one.
